cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Co-Sign This
cards.instruction: Get someone to help by making them an official participant who shares responsibility for the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Could you co-sign the form for borrowing this barbecue?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll help carry it. That handle looks cracked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Good eye. Sign as joint custodian; we'll inspect it together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The owner wants a replacement by Sunday if it breaks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're co-chair of replacements too. I'll call the shops; you approve what we buy before either of us promises her anything.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 appoints joint custodian and A5 co-chair, retaining A participation; A1 co-sign request is softened and status mostly in repetitive prefixes.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cracked handle causes A3 shared inspection; B4 Sunday replacement condition causes A5 shared purchase decisions and promises.

relationship.evidence: B2 volunteers carrying and notices damage; B4 owner demand changes the joint risk rather than merely resisting.

heightening.evidence: A5 extends B4 liability into official replacement participation while A calls shops, deepening shared responsibility.
